content.value_statement: React components can become hard to maintain when effects, refs, and state patterns are misused. This skill gives concise React guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to avoid effects and calculate values during render.
Shows safer useEffect dependencies, cleanup, and updater function patterns.
Guides ref usage for DOM access, timers, and dynamic lists.
Compares controlled, uncontrolled, compound, and composed component patterns.
Provides React code examples for common hook and component decisions.
limitations: Does not run tests, lint code, or inspect dependencies by itself.
Does not replace official React documentation for version-specific API details.
Focuses on component patterns, not routing, build tooling, or deployment.
Assumes the user provides relevant React files or component context.

use_cases.title: Refactor Effect-heavy Components
use_cases.description: Review components that overuse useEffect and move derived logic into render or event handlers.

use_cases.title: Teach Hook Decisions
use_cases.description: Create review guidance that explains when to use useMemo, refs, useEffectEvent, or direct calculation.

use_cases.title: Review Reusable UI APIs
use_cases.description: Assess component props, composition, controlled state, and provider boundaries before expanding shared UI.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for effect, state, ref, and composition issues. Explain each change in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite an Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this component to remove unnecessary useEffect usage. Keep behavior the same and explain what now runs during render or events.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a focused custom hook for this React behavior. Make dependencies explicit and avoid lifecycle-style wrappers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Component API
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this reusable component API for prop complexity, composition options, controlled state, and provider boundaries. Recommend a maintainable design.

output_examples.input: A product page shows notifications from an effect when cart state changes.
output_examples.output: Move the notification into the purchase event handler so it only runs for the user's action.

output_examples.input: A chat component reconnects every time a theme prop changes.
output_examples.output: Keep the connection effect tied to the room and read the latest theme through non-reactive effect logic.

output_examples.input: A reusable panel has many boolean props that switch large UI branches.
output_examples.output: Split the branches into composed components and keep shared state behind a scoped provider when needed.

best_practices: Ask whether logic can run during render before adding an effect.
Keep effect dependency lists honest and fix code instead of suppressing the linter.
Use composition and controlled state when a component must support varied behavior.
anti_patterns: Using effects to mirror derived state that can be calculated directly.
Creating lifecycle-style hooks that hide dependencies from React lint rules.
Adding many boolean props to one component instead of composing separate variants.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when reviewing or writing React components, especially files that use hooks, refs, or reusable UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript React?
faq.answer: Yes. It pairs well with TypeScript guidance and applies to TSX and JSX component work.

faq.question: Can it fix React code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples. The AI assistant still needs file context and permission to edit code.

faq.question: Does it cover React Server Components?
faq.answer: No. The included guidance focuses on client component patterns, effects, refs, hooks, and composition.

faq.question: Why does it discourage many effects?
faq.answer: Many effects duplicate render logic or event logic. Avoiding them reduces bugs, extra renders, and stale dependency issues.

faq.question: Is it safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed files are documentation only. The audit found no real command execution or reconnaissance behavior.
